mountain belt, known as Fibulheimen is considered to be a part of the Circum

included in Fibulheimen are as shown in the Fig.1. The area described as

Muhlig-Hoffmanfjella to the west. 
The Wohlthat range on the  east, is a Proterozoic high grade metamorphic 
terrain with associated complex metamorphic, migmatitic, magmatic and de-
formation history comparable with other mountain ranges of Fibulheimen 
mountain belt. The area was first described by Ravich and Soloviev(l 966) and 
was subsequently studied by Indian geologists. The Wohlthat region exposes 
high grade ortho and para gneisses in Humboldt, Pe termann and Schirmacher 
area (Sengupta,1988; Pant,1991; Joshi et al,  1991; Ravindra et al.,  1994 and

with an overprint of amphibolite facies. The  major manifestation of magmatic 
phase in Wohlthat range is in the form of a large Anorthosite massif in Gruber 
area (Ravich & Kamanev, 1975; Kaul et al., 1991), foliated opx  bearing granites 
(charnockites) from Skeids area, Charnockite suite rocks from Petermann 
ranges (Joshi & Pant; 1995), alkali granites from Petermann and Skeids area 
and charnockite-granite in intrusives from northern Humboldt (Ra vindra & 
Kaul, 1995). 
The Muhlig-Hoffmanfjella ranges on the west, mainly exposes metasu-
pracrustals comprising of migmatites, felsic gneisses and pelitic-semipelitic 
gneisses with intrusive gab bros (Ohta  et al., 1990; Buc her-Nurminen & Ohta, 
1993). However the most domi nant lithounits exposed in this region are the 
batholithic charnockites with some granites. 
The geology of the other parts of Fibulheimen i.e. Sverdrup fjella and 
Sor-Rondanfjella have been comprehensively described (Groenwald & Hunter, 
1991; Allen, 1991 and Shiraishi  et al, 1991). The outc rops in  Sor-Rondanfjella 
comprise of high grade metamorphic rocks, associated plutoni c rocks and minor 
Mesozoic dykes. The H.U. Sverdrupfjella ranges expose mainly a s equence of 
para and orthogneiss and are suggestively products of regressive rehydration 
from granulite facies assemblages. Also occurring in the region are the younger 
alkaline p lutonic complex and dole rite dykes related to extensional environ-
ment generated during the Gondwana rifting. 
Geological Setting 
On the basis of the field setting and petrographical characteristics, the rocks 
exposed in Dallmannfjellet area have been divided into three majo r units 
(Fig.2), as given below. 
(i) Metamorphi tes: Comprising layered heterogeneous garn et-biotite bear-
ing quartzo-feldspathic gneisses, garnet-sillimanite-codierite gneisses, 
granulite-amphibolite bands, garnetiferous pyroxene granulites and 
gneisses and bands of marble and calc- silicate rocks. Minor orthogneis-
sic rocks of tonalitic to granitic composition also occur. Compositional 
heterogeneity exhibited  through pronounced layering (Figs 3 and 4) is 
seen in the exposed rock at any given location. These rocks are domi-
nantly exposed along the eas tern ridge of the mapped area and also 
possibly as a restitic phase within the charnockite and granite. 
(ii) Foliated charnockite: It is exposed in the wes tern outcrop of the area 
mapped and is closely associated with  layered para and orthogneisses.
